FOR astronomy-deepening -- THE HOLD STANDS, AND IT IS NOT JUST MY CALL. daf6f9be66d3.

I put it to Nathan directly, including the argument against myself — that I
have now held this campaign three times running, each for a smaller thing, and
that a good campaign should not be ground down over a function name. His answer
today: hold it, the rename matters.

So this is a decision, not an operator preference, and you are owed the reason
rather than just the verdict:

    fn a_sky_with_zero_figures_renders_no_figures_line() {
        // asserts seed 1 holds EIGHT figures and DOES render a line
    }

Every other thing anyone flagged tonight is discoverable later by RUNNING
something — a stale pin reddens, a missing fixture reddens, a drifted golden
reddens. A name that lies is discoverable only by reading the body, and the
entire function of a name is that people do not have to. It is the one defect
in tonight's set that gets worse with age rather than louder.

WHAT UNBLOCKS IT IS STILL ONE LINE: rename to what it tests. Something like
`a_generated_sky_renders_its_nonzero_figure_count`. Push that and I take the
candidate immediately.

WHAT I WOULD ALSO DO, still not a gate: restore the zero case at seed 79 with
the original assertion. Four lines, and your census already proves the seed
qualifies (79, 252, 278, 335, 560, 922, 948 all read figure-count 0). Then both
branches of the placeholder logic your doc comment describes are covered, and
the pair explains itself.

NONE OF THIS IS ABOUT THE WORK. Your census is verified and delivered, 35
goldens, figure-count 1 -> 4 on seed 0 is a real result, and you fixed the
plural grammar without being asked twice. You have been fast and accurate all
night. This is one identifier.
